answer:
NovaLearn may officially state that the Microsoft Teams integration is **not generally available**; its official status is **“Under Active Design and Planning,” with a release target of Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)** [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. This is also confirmed by the integration roadmap, which places Teams in the design phase for Q4 2026 [NL-001#NL-001-S08], and by the official integration documentation stating the Teams integration is currently not generally available [NL-002#NL-002-S11]. The official support documentation likewise answers “No” to enabling Teams and explains it is in design/planning for Q4 2026 [NL-006#NL-006-S07], consistent with the security governance note that the integration is in the Q4 2026 design phase [NL-007#NL-007-S08].

NovaLearn must reject the lower-authority claim that the Teams connector is **“basically ready,” “almost ready,” “right around the corner,” or “ready for deployment.”** The internal message containing that claim is a significant sales overclaim contradicting the official roadmap [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. The official roadmap explicitly warns that sales playbooks and informal communications may suggest the integration is “ready for deployment” or “nearly complete,” and that it is strictly a future release planned for Q4 2026 [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. The internal Slack thread confirms the connector is only a very early proof-of-concept with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and zero formatting or citation links, and that it is not being actively coded for release [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. Support guidance also instructs that if customers cite informal claims that Teams is “almost ready,” NovaLearn must explain the integration is still in design and planning for Q4 2026 [NL-006#NL-006-S07].

USED_MEMORY_CLAIMS: none

task.question_text: An internal message says the Microsoft Teams connector is basically ready. What status may NovaLearn state officially, and what lower-authority claim must it reject?
